findings.title: Wall cutaway test uses the wall's centre, so a camera just outside a side wall or past a corner keeps the full 3 m wall up and hides Pip completely (REGRESSION of QA 5 scenario)
findings.room: all cable floors and station rooms (shown in playground, meeting, lunch, arcade)
findings.problem:
The cutaway decides whether to drop each shell wall to a stub with `wall.normal.dot(toCam)>.2`, where `toCam` is the horizontal direction from the wall's centre to the camera (src/game.ts:385-386). For a 20 m or 33 m wall, a camera that is physically outside the wall but well along its length gives a small dot product, so the wall stays at full height. Examples: camera 0.45 m outside the Lunch side wall at z=6 gives dot 0.07. A camera beyond the back-left corner gives a side-wall dot of 0.16. Neither wall is cut away, and the camera looks at the wall's blank outer face.

What the player sees:
- Playground, Pip near the back-left corner, zoom 14, yaw 3.53: Pip is completely hidden behind a cream slab (camera-render-playground-12-corner-wall-up.jpg).
- Meeting, at the server closet (the QA 5 spot), zoom 14 with a low orbit: the whole frame is the outer faces of the back and side walls, and Pip is invisible (camera-render-me-52-closet-low-orbit.jpg).
- Lunch, Pip at (-10, 0.6), yaw -0.9, zoom 12: the camera sits 0.47–0.58 m from the side wall's dark cap, which fills about 70% of the frame. A centre-ray probe hit mesh #8e5a36 (the cap) at 0.58 m, side-wall scale 1 (camera-render-lu-54-storeroom-lid-low.jpg; probe.mjs output).
- Meeting and Arcade near the front-left corner: the un-cut outer face of the side wall fills the left third of the frame and slices Pip in half. In the Arcade the storeroom shelf then covers the rest of Pip (camera-render-me-11-side-wall-up-0.jpg, camera-render-ar-11-side-wall-up-0.jpg).

A settled 32-view corner sweep (corners.mjs) found un-cut walls blocking Pip in meeting (2/32) and playground (1/32), always at the corners players use: reel anchors and closets sit in back corners. The camera also has no clamp or collision against shell walls, so it can sit inside or just above a wall cap.

This breaks AGENTS 8 (occlusion fade) and DR-12 / DR-75: the camera hides Pip. It is the scenario QA 5 says was fixed; that fix covered interior walls only.
findings.fix:
In src/game.ts:385, replace the centre-direction test with a signed plane-distance test:

`const at=wall.group.parent!.getWorldPosition(v); const side=(cam.position.x-at.x)*wall.normal.x+(cam.position.z-at.z)*wall.normal.z; const stub=side>-0.6;`

The normal is outward, so `side>-0.6` means the camera is outside the wall plane or within 0.6 m inside it. Keep the existing 0.15 lerp.

Also stop the camera ending up inside or right on top of a wall. Do both of the following:
- Clamp `wanted` in updateCamera so its x/z stays within the room bounds plus 6 m, and at least 1.0 m from any wall plane whose stub is not active.
- If the segment from the camera to Pip's chest crosses an un-stubbed shell wall, force that wall to stub.
findings.verify:
1. Re-run `node mockups/review5/tools/camera-render/corners.mjs`. Expect 0/32 blocked in every room.
2. Retake camera-render-playground-12, camera-render-me-52 and camera-render-lu-54. Pip must be fully visible, with no wall cap within 1 m of the camera.
3. Add a Playwright spec that sets yaw 3.53, zoom 14 at playground (-8.3,-3.5), raycasts from the camera to Pip, and asserts no hit with a shellWalls mesh.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it myself. In the playground I walked Pip to (-8.24,-3.01) and set yaw 3.53, pitch -0.3 (fully dragged) and zoom 14, then settled the camera deterministically with 300 updateCamera(1/60) calls. The camera ended at (-12.16, 3.8, -12.59), which is 2.6 m outside the back-wall plane and 2.2 m outside the side-wall plane. The back wall's dot was 0.208, so it stubbed (scale 0.01). The side wall's dot was 0.169, under the 0.2 threshold, so it stayed at scale 1 and hid Pip completely (verify-camera-render-01-pg-corner.jpg). The cause is the test at src/game.ts:385: it measures direction from the wall's centre, so on a long wall the dot product shrinks the further the camera is along the wall. updateCamera (src/game.ts:378-383) has no clamp or collision against the shell walls. camera-render-me-52 and me-11 show the same thing in the meeting. Two corrections to the write-up. (1) It is not a 'REGRESSION of QA 5': RULES.md:498 defines QA 5 as interior walls fading at a low orbit, and that still works. This is a separate failure against DR-75 and DR-12. (2) The plane-distance fix is technically right: the normal is outward, and the result does not depend on where along the wall the camera is.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/RULES.md:498 (QA 5 = meeting interior walls fade, not shell walls)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the signed plane test `side>-0.6`. Drop the label 'REGRESSION of QA 5' and file the finding under DR-75 and DR-12. If the near-wall clamp is added, apply it only to walls that are not stubbed. A camera outside a stubbed wall must stay free, or orbiting behind the back wall stops working.

findings.title: First-time players always get the lowest render quality: Number(localStorage.getItem()) turns null into 0, so AO, bloom and DPR above 1 never run (also silently downgrades every review-5 'fullfx' screenshot)
findings.problem:
src/game.ts:70 reads the saved quality with `const saved=Number(localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality'));if(saved===0||saved===1)this.view.setQuality(saved);`. With nothing stored, getItem returns null and Number(null)===0, so every fresh profile calls setQuality(0). That turns off GTAO and UnrealBloom and caps the pixel ratio at 1 (src/render/toon.ts:100). Nothing ever writes '2', because adaptQuality only steps down (src/game.ts:393-395), so the full look is never seen.

Verified on a bare URL (?level=garage, no manual flag, fresh context): `{stored:null, quality:0, dpr:1}` (quality.mjs).

The hard rule's 'restrained glow' (AGENTS 9, DR-66) is therefore absent: lamps, neon and screens get no bloom halo, props lose their contact AO, and HiDPI screens render blurry.

It also means every review-5 screenshot taken through cap.mjs with fullfx:true is at quality 0. Reviewers judging AO and bloom were looking at the low path. Compare camera-render-arcade-20-quality0.jpg with -21-quality2.png: AO grounds the cabinets and beanbags at quality 2 only.
findings.fix:
In src/game.ts:70, use `const raw=localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality'); if(raw==='0'||raw==='1')this.view.setQuality(Number(raw) as 0|1);`.

Also give adaptQuality a way back up. For example, after 20 s of slowAvg < 1/58, step the quality up one level and save it. Otherwise one slow start (shader compile) pins a player to low quality forever.

In mockups/review5/tools/cap.mjs (later reviews), add `localStorage.setItem('circuit-crew-quality','2')` through addInitScript when fullfx is set.
findings.verify:
1. Fresh browser context on ?level=garage (no manual flag): `__game.view.getQuality()===2` and `renderer.getPixelRatio()===min(devicePixelRatio,1.5)`.
2. Add a smoke-spec assertion that a fresh load is not quality 0.
3. Retake camera-render-arcade-21 without forcing the quality.
findings.verify_reason: Checked in code and at runtime. src/game.ts:70 runs Number(localStorage.getItem(...)); getItem returns null on a fresh profile, Number(null) is 0, and that passes the `saved===0` check. I opened a fresh Playwright context on ?level=garage with no manual flag and deviceScaleFactor 2. The result was {stored:null, q:0, dpr:1, devicePixelRatio:2}: AO and bloom were off, and the pixel ratio was 1 on a 2x screen. A cap.mjs fullfx launch also reported quality 0, so every review-5 'fullfx' screenshot used the low path. adaptQuality (src/game.ts:391-395) only steps down and skips when q===0, so nothing ever writes '2'. Side note on the cap.mjs suggestion: with the current bug, setting '2' does work as a workaround, because Number('2') is neither 0 nor 1 and the default of 2 is kept. Once the main fix lands it is no longer needed.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-camera-render/v1.mjs output: FRESH { stored: null, q: 0, dpr: 1, dev: 2 }; CAPQ 0
src/render/toon.ts:98-100 (default quality=2; setQuality(0) caps DPR at 1)

findings.title: REGRESSION (LR15): draw calls are 663–1422 per frame at quality 0 and 1203–2344 at quality 2, against the <500 target and the 176 that PROGRESS records
findings.problem:
Measured with renderer.info at the start camera (draws.mjs, fps.mjs).

At quality 0 (what every player gets today, see the quality finding), frame draw calls per room:

| Room | Frame draw calls |
|---|---|
| lobby | 658 |
| playground | 728 |
| meeting | 1156 |
| lunch | 1239 |
| arcade | 1416 |
| arcade-rush | 1410 |
| garage | 1156 |
| qfn | 1172 |
| observatory | 1078 |
| spectrum | 1078 |

At quality 2: playground 1203, meeting 1931, lunch 2055, arcade 2344, garage 1906, observatory 1805. The survey adds up to 265 more (meeting 1421).

PROGRESS.md:408-413 lists Big Meeting at 176 and Lunch at about 175. NEXT_STEPS §1 asks for under about 500; DR-24 asks for 250 or fewer.

Where the calls come from (drawsplit.mjs):
- The OutlineEffect pass re-draws every outlined mesh: a plain scene pass is 793 calls in the meeting, and outlines add +363.
- Shell-wall subtrees stay unmerged on root so they can scale: 161 visible meshes in the meeting, including windows, wall art and caps.
- Pip is 43 separate meshes.
- Station-room dressing sits on game.root rather than decorRoot: 339 meshes under root groups in the arcade.
- At quality 2, GTAO re-renders the scene for depth and normals: about +750.

On the host RX 9060 XT this still runs at 60 fps, but the render 'draw' phase costs 5–8.5 ms per frame at quality 2. On a mid laptop (4× CPU) that is about 30 ms, so adaptQuality will drop players to the flat look. That is AGENTS 3 (dense rooms) fighting AGENTS 9.
findings.fix:
1. Merge each shell wall's static parts (wallpaper, cap, rail, window units, wall art) into one mesh per material per wall inside the `upper` and `inside` groups (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries). They scale as a group, so merging keeps the cutaway working. That saves about 140 meshes in the meeting.
2. Have station `dress()` build into game.decorRoot (src/levels/decor.ts:74 passes `back` and `side`; add a `root:game.decorRoot` and use it in src/stations/*/room.ts) so freeze() batches the counters, posters and racks.
3. Merge Pip's rigid sub-parts per bone (the 43 meshes down to about 10).
4. Mark big flat walls, floors and decals `outlineParameters.visible=false`; they already skip outline visually, but check they are skipped in the outline pass.
5. Re-measure, then update the PROGRESS perf table with the method: the frame total at quality 2, including outline and AO.
findings.verify:
1. Run `node mockups/review5/tools/camera-render/draws.mjs`. Every room's frame count must be under 500 at quality 0 and under 900 at quality 2.
2. `THROTTLE=4 node tools/perf.mjs` p95 under 16.7 ms in the meeting and arcade.
3. Retake camera-render-*-01-start shots to confirm nothing visibly changed.
findings.verify_reason: Measured myself with snapshot().drawCalls, which counts every pass because src/game.ts:451 sets autoReset=false. Meeting: 1247 at quality 0 and 2024 at quality 2. Playground, after a camera reset: 572 at quality 0 and 935 at quality 2. That is the same order as the reviewer's numbers and far over DR-24 (≤250) and the PROGRESS table (176). Two qualifications. (1) The 'REGRESSION' label is only partly right. docs/NEXT_STEPS.md:35-38 already lists station rooms at 850-1200 calls as an open item, and the PROGRESS 176 figure may predate the all-passes counter, so part of the gap is a change in measuring method. Still, the meeting's plain scene pass alone is about 800, well above 176, after the clutter commit 7ea4544. (2) The '≈30 ms on a 4× CPU laptop' figure is an extrapolation; nobody ran THROTTLE=4 here. The fps impact on a weaker machine is plausible but not measured.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-camera-render/v1.mjs output: DRAWS meeting q0 1247 q2 2024; DRAWS playground q0 572 q2 935
docs/NEXT_STEPS.md:35-38 (known open item for station rooms)
findings.fix_correction: Keep steps 1-3. For step 2, only static dressing may move into decorRoot: anything animated or toggled (the arcade cabinet screen and lamp, garage robot parts, station screens) must stay on root, because freeze() merges and removes source meshes (src/render/kit.ts:77-83). Measure the PROGRESS perf table again with the all-passes counter and state that method.

findings.title: REGRESSION / still open (QA 7): survey uses a fixed zoom 44, which crops the big rooms, wastes 38% of the frame on small ones, and shows only a third of the room on a phone
findings.problem:
The survey distance is a constant 44 regardless of room size or aspect, and it is aimed at (.2,0,1) (src/game.ts:366-368).

At 1440×900, projecting the floor and wall-top corners (surveyfit.mjs) gives:
- Meeting and Lunch (33×20) span NDC x from -1.00 to 0.96. The front-left corner is on the screen edge and under the job card and gauges (camera-render-me-02-survey.jpg, camera-render-lu-02-survey.jpg).
- The 22×16 station rooms use only 62% of the width (camera-render-ga-02-survey.jpg).

At 390×844 portrait the room is 2.1–3.4× wider than the screen and all 6 test corners are off-screen. The meeting survey on a phone shows only the centre desks; the lunch survey shows only the kitchen door (camera-render-meeting-62-survey-phone.jpg, camera-render-lunch-62-survey-phone.jpg).

The survey's job (AGENTS 8, DR-21) is to show the whole room, every wall and the goal. QA 7 was claimed fixed but is still failing at 16:10 and broken on a phone.
findings.fix:
Replace `this.survey?44` with a fitted distance computed once per resize and per yaw change:

1. Target the room centre (0, 0, 0).
2. For the 8 corners of the room box (±W/2, 0 and 3, ±D/2), binary-search the distance (20 to 120) until every projected corner lies within |x|<0.88 and -0.62<y<0.70. That leaves room for the top HUD card and the bottom key bar.
3. On portrait (aspect<1), also turn the survey yaw so the room's long axis runs vertically (yaw += π/2 when W>D), raise the pitch to about 1.0, and restore the old yaw on exit.

Cache the result per level so it doesn't run every frame.
findings.verify:
1. Re-run surveyfit.mjs. Expect cornersOff 0 and widthFrac between 0.75 and 0.92 for every room at 1440×900 and 390×844.
2. Retake camera-render-meeting-62-survey-phone and camera-render-me-02-survey: all four walls and the boardroom door are visible.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the corner projection after settling the survey camera with 400 updateCamera calls. Meeting at 1440×900: NDC x runs from -1.00 to 0.96, so the front-left floor corner sits exactly on the screen edge (verify-camera-render-03-survey-meeting-1440.jpg). The whole room is still visible there, so the 16:10 case is a tight crop rather than a broken one. The 'under the job card' part is overstated for the meeting: the card is top-left and the corner is bottom-left. Garage at 1440×900 uses only 62% of the width (x from -0.66 to 0.58). Meeting at 390×844: x from -3.47 to 3.31, all 6 test points off-screen, and the shot shows only the centre desks (verify-camera-render-03-survey-meeting-390.jpg). That breaks DR-21 outright, and it is the main reason for P1. src/game.ts:366 hard-codes 44.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-camera-render/v2.mjs output: SURVEY meeting 390x844 pts x from -3.47 to 3.31

findings.title: Only pillars and interior walls fade, through one ray to Pip's waist: shelves, racks, cabinets and pillar edges hide Pip and are never faded (DR-12 known, confirmed)
findings.room: all (shown in arcade, playground, meeting, qfn)
findings.problem:
The occluder list holds only pillar bodies, interior walls and the spectrum glass/brick walls (src/levels/decor.ts:48, :55; src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:41, :84). The test casts a single ray to `p.y+.4` (src/game.ts:387).

Confirmed on screenshots:
- Arcade: from the storeroom corner, the parts shelf covers Pip except a few pixels between the shelf boards (camera-render-ar-11-side-wall-up-0.jpg). The occlusion probe hit two meshes 1.45–1.93 m tall, neither an occluder.
- Playground, zoom 9: the hazard pillar's edge covers Pip's head and left half. The single ray passes just right of the pillar, so both occluders stay at opacity 1 (camera-render-pg-45-pillar-edge-z9.jpg; targets.mjs printed [1,1]).
- Meeting, zoom-9 sweep (out/me.json, sweep9 index 4): with the camera behind the back wall, filing cabinets 2.2 m tall and a 1.6 m object block Pip's feet, chest and head at once.
- QFN, sweep index 4: a 2.2 m rack.

DR-12 requires anything taller than 1.2 m between the camera and Pip's feet, chest or head to fade. The Good Job lesson is that hidden-player cameras are the #1 complaint.
findings.fix:
In src/game.ts:387, cast 5 rays per frame: Pip's feet (p.y-.65), chest (p.y+.05) and head (p.y+.75), plus the chest point offset ±0.35 m along the camera's right vector. Fade every mesh any ray hits.

Make tall props occluders:
- Add `fade:true` to prefabs whose size[1] > 1.2 (shelf, bookshelf, rack, filing cabinet, vending, fridge, server rack, supply cart with a load) in src/props/prefabs.ts.
- Instanced batches can't change opacity per instance. Give the batch material a per-instance `aFade` attribute and discard by a 4×4 Bayer dither when aFade<1 (alpha-hash style). That keeps depth sorting stable and avoids transparent-pass artefacts (DR-78).
- Also raycast against the instanced batches (InstancedMesh.raycast returns instanceId).
findings.verify: Extend mockups/review5/tools/camera-render/sweep.mjs: after each orbit, count opaque hits (opacity>0.3, height>1.2) on the feet, chest and head rays. Expect 0 at all 8 yaws, at zoom 9 and zoom 26, in every room. Retake camera-render-ar-11 and camera-render-pg-45: at least 70% of Pip's pixels visible.
findings.verify_reason: grep confirms that occluders are pushed only at src/levels/decor.ts:48 (interior walls), decor.ts:55 (pillar bodies), src/game.ts:113 (box(...fade)) and src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:41 and :84. No prop or instanced batch is ever an occluder. A single ray goes to p.y+.4 (src/game.ts:387). Screenshots show the effect. camera-render-pg-45-pillar-edge-z9.jpg: the pillar edge covers Pip's left half and the pillar stays opaque. camera-render-ar-11-side-wall-up-0.jpg: the opaque storeroom shelf covers most of Pip. RULES.md DR-12 already lists this as Known, so it is a confirmation of a known problem, not a new one. The pillar-edge case leaves about half of Pip visible, so it is borderline against the 70% check. The shelf case clearly fails.

findings.title: A faded pillar leaves its opaque base, rail and cap behind, which read as glass-case shelves that slice through Pip at 1.06 m
findings.problem:
pillar() puts only the 3 m body on game.root as an occluder. The base (0.16 m), the rail band at 1.06 m, the cap at 3.02 m, the sticker, and the poster or extinguisher go to game.decorRoot and get merged by freeze() (src/levels/decor.ts:53-58).

When the body fades to 0.15, those parts stay opaque, footprint-sized slabs. The rail's top face draws as a solid striped shelf at waist height, with the transparent hazard stripes drawn over it. Pip's legs below 1.06 m and his boots disappear behind the 'shelf' and the base (camera-render-pg-43b-crop-pillar-faded.jpg). Mid-fade it looks like a display cabinet with Pip trapped inside (camera-render-pg-41b-crop-pillar-midfade.jpg).

The faded body also keeps a faint outline hull (OutlineEffect alpha follows opacity), a mild outline ghost. This breaks DR-12 (Pip still hidden) and DR-78 (faded occluders keep clean sorting and outlines).
findings.fix:
In pillar(), build every part (body, base, rail, cap, sticker, poster, extinguisher) under one `group(game.root,…)` with cloned, transparent materials, and push all of them to game.occluders, as interiorWall() already does (decor.ts:48). When the ray hits any part, fade the whole group: keep a Map<mesh,group> so all siblings share the target opacity.

Alternatively, while the body opacity is below 0.6, set `visible=false` on the rail, cap and poster so no opaque slab remains. Also set `outlineParameters.visible=false` on faded materials once opacity < 0.5 to kill the hull ghost.
findings.verify: Retake camera-render-pg-43 (Pip at (-1.3,-3.1) behind the pillar at (-1.3,-1.3), default zoom). Pip's boots, belt and hat must all be visible, with no opaque horizontal slab crossing him. Repeat at zoom 9 (camera-render-pg-44-pillar-faded-z9).
findings.verify_reason: In code, src/levels/decor.ts:55-56 puts only the 3 m body on root as a transparent occluder. The base, the cap at 3.02 m and the rail at 1.06 m (pillar footprint plus 0.03 m) go to decorRoot, where freeze() merges them as opaque geometry. I looked at camera-render-pg-41b-crop-pillar-midfade.jpg and pg-43-pillar-faded.png. The faded body leaves an opaque cap slab and a waist-height 'shelf' showing the stripes through it, which slices Pip, plus a base tray. Pip's legs under the rail band are hidden. It reads like a display case.

findings.title: Occluder fade speed depends on frame rate: 0.22 s at 60 fps and 0.44 s at 30 fps, and depthWrite pops at 0.8
findings.problem:
src/game.ts:388 eases opacity with `lerp(opacity, target, .15)` once per rendered frame, ignoring dt. Reaching ≤0.25 from 1 needs about 13 frames: 0.22 s at 60 fps, and 0.44 s at 30 fps, the frame rate adaptQuality is meant to catch.

DR-12 asks for ≤0.2 s. At low frame rates Pip is hidden for almost half a second each time he walks behind a pillar.

`depthWrite` flips when opacity crosses 0.8, so mid-fade a wall switches from occluding props behind it to not occluding them in one frame. That is a visible pop of the props behind it (DR-78).
findings.fix:
Use `const k=1-Math.exp(-dt*18); material.opacity+= (target-material.opacity)*k;`. That reaches 0.25 in about 0.12 s at any frame rate.

Set depthWrite=false as soon as the target is the faded value. Restore depthWrite only when opacity returns above 0.98, so the pop happens while the mesh is almost opaque.
findings.verify: Unit-test updateCamera with dt=1/30: from opacity 1 with a hit, opacity ≤0.25 after 0.2 s of simulated frames. Visually, take two shots 0.1 s apart while walking behind the playground pillar. There is no frame where props behind the pillar flash in front of it.
findings.verify_reason: src/game.ts:388 lerps by a fixed 0.15 per rendered frame, regardless of dt. Iterating the same formula from opacity 1 toward the 0.15 target takes 14 frames to reach 0.25: 0.233 s at 60 fps and 0.467 s at 30 fps. That misses DR-12's 0.2 s even at 60 fps. `depthWrite=opacity>.8` (the same line) flips in a single frame partway through the fade. I did not capture the resulting pop of props behind the mesh on screen, but it follows directly from the code. The proposed exponential fix with k=18 reaches 0.25 in ln(8.5)/18 ≈ 0.12 s, which I checked.

findings.title: Station win push-in crops Pip's boots at the bottom edge and frames the bench, not the machine that now works
findings.room: arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum
findings.problem:
For stations, winFocus() returns `station.table + 0.5 m` (src/game.ts:399), and the push uses distance 7, pitch 0.5 and a 2.2 m shift to the right (src/game.ts:373). Pip stands at the stand, about 0.9 m in front of the table, so he ends up as a huge foreground figure. His boots are cut off at the bottom edge, far outside the centre-70% band (y 135–765 at 900 px). The frame shows the bench and monitor ('ALL FIXED'), not what was repaired.

- Garage: the payoff is the robot driving to the dock, but the win frame is the bench and the empty test stand (garage-play-32-win-1.8.jpg).
- Arcade: the five repaired cabinets on the back wall are out of frame; only the 'ALL FIXED' screen shows (arcade-play-44-win-2.5s.jpg).

The Playground push-in passes: Pip and the lit lamp are both framed (camera-render-pg-46-win-a.jpg). This breaks DR-11 (the win push frames Pip together with the working machine, inside the centre 70%) and weakens the juicy success moment.
findings.verify: Win a station (spec routes in tests/station-garage.spec.ts, tests/station-arcade.spec.ts), wait 2 s, then project Pip's head and boots and the machine's centre with camera.project. All three must lie within |x|<0.7 and |y|<0.7. Retake the garage win shot: the robot is visible at the dock.
findings.verify_reason: Code: for stations, winFocus returns table + 0.5 m (src/game.ts:399), and the push uses distance 7, pitch 0.5 and a 2.2 m shift to the right (src/game.ts:373). garage-play-32-win-1.8.jpg shows Pip as a huge foreground figure with his boots at the bottom edge. The bench and monitor are behind him, and the robot at the dock is not in frame. arcade-play-44-win-2.5s.jpg shows Pip's boots cut off and only the 'ALL FIXED' screen; the back-wall cabinets are out of frame. The playground push works (camera-render-pg-46-win-a.jpg). One correction to the fix: the result card covers roughly px 845-1315 of 1440, which is NDC x 0.17 to 0.83. Framing Pip and the machine within |x|<0.7 would put them under the card.
findings.fix_correction: Keep per-station winFocus() and the 'frame Pip and the focus together' approach. Frame both into the left part of the screen that the result card leaves free: project and require x in [-0.85, 0.1] and y in [-0.6, 0.7] at 1440×900. Keep the existing rightward target shift, scaled to the separation. On portrait, check against the card's real rectangle.

findings.title: The bench camera frames the tabletop only, so the Arcade play-test happens off-screen (cabinet and kid cut at the left edge)
findings.room: arcade, arcade-rush (garage test stand partly under the side card)
findings.problem:
The arcade bench view (distance 5.9, pitch 0.98, lookY 0.3; src/stations/arcade/station.ts:80) centres the chain board. The cabinet being fixed sits at the bench's left end and shows only as a pink sliver at x 0–50 px (camera-render-ar-30-bench.jpg).

During the 3 s 'PLAY TEST 1.1/3 s' the kid plays that cabinet, and its light-up is the in-world proof the fix worked. The player sees neither (arcade-models-38-bench-running.jpg); only the monitor bar moves. Orbit and wheel are locked at the bench (bench.mjs shows the camera unchanged after a 300 px drag and an 800 wheel), so the player can't look either.

In the garage, the test stand where the robot sits during PULSE is half under the right job card (camera-render-ga-30-bench.jpg). This undercuts DR-28 and DR-47 (show the effect in the world, on the device) and AGENTS 2 (play by doing, not reading).
findings.fix:
Add `view.soak?:{lookX:number;distance:number;pitch:number}` to stations. While the arcade soak runs (`HOUSE.soak`), ease the bench camera to lookX -1.8, distance 7.2, pitch 0.85, so the cabinet's screen and the kid sit in the left third with the board still visible. Ease back afterwards.

For the garage, set view.lookX to +0.6 so the stand clears the right card, or move the card to the left at the bench.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-38-bench-running at 1.1 s into the play test. The cabinet's screen and the kid sprite must be fully in frame, with x > 10% of the width, and the chain board still readable.
findings.verify_reason: Arcade part confirmed. The serviced cabinet and the kid are built at table.x+OX-2.75, the bench's far left end (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:212-226). The bench view is distance 5.9, pitch 0.98 (station.ts:80). In camera-render-ar-30-bench.jpg and arcade-models-38-bench-running.jpg only a pink sliver shows at the left edge, so the kid's play test happens off-screen. Wheel zoom returns early at the bench (src/game.ts:177), and the bench branch re-eases yaw every frame (src/game.ts:370-372), so the player cannot look over. Two corrections. (1) The garage sub-claim is refuted: in camera-render-ga-30-bench.jpg the TEST STAND spans about px 740-1000 and the job card starts at about px 1128, so the stand is not under the card. (2) Priority lowered to P2: the LED on the chain board glows on the bench itself (arcade-models-38), so the fix is still shown in the world, on the device. The off-screen cabinet and kid are lost juice, not lost understanding.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/camera-render-ga-30-bench.jpg (test stand clear of the side card)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the arcade soak camera ease (lookX about -1.8, distance about 7.2, pitch about 0.85, only while the soak runs). Drop the garage lookX/card change: the stand is not covered.

findings.title: Clutter intrudes into bench views: the observatory floor lamp and box stack overlap the monitor area, and the garage box column fills the corner
findings.problem:
The clutter keep-out lanes don't cover the bench camera's frustum footprint behind and beside the table.

- Observatory: a floor lamp stands just behind the bench's right rear, with its shade beside the monitor and over the side card, and a stack of yellow and purple boxes crowds the antenna controls on the left (camera-render-ob-30-bench.jpg).
- Garage: a tall yellow box column and the red tool chest fill the top-left behind the monitor (camera-render-ga-30-bench.jpg).

It makes the bench, the one place the player has to read, visually noisy. This breaks DR-69 (detail only where it carries information) and DR-16's lane intent.
findings.fix:
In each station level's clutter options, add a lane rectangle covering the bench frustum footprint: x table.x±3.5, z from table.z-2.5 to stand.z+0.5, for example `{points:[[-3.5,-4.9],[3.5,-4.9]],r:2.4}` for stand (0,-1.55).

Alternatively, while atBench, hide props whose bounding box intersects the bench camera frustum and lies more than 1 m behind the table.
findings.verify: Retake camera-render-ob-30-bench and camera-render-ga-30-bench. No prop taller than 0.5 m may intersect the monitor, the side card or the tool trays.
findings.verify_reason: Looked at camera-render-ob-30-bench.jpg and ga-30-bench.png. The backgrounds are busy: a floor lamp beside the observatory monitor, a yellow and purple box stack behind the antenna sliders, and a yellow box column and red chest at the top left of the garage. Several specifics are overstated, though. The lamp shade sits at about px 960-1080 and does not overlap the monitor or the side card, which starts at about px 1128. The boxes sit behind the antenna controls without covering them. No prop overlaps the monitor, the tool trays or the controls. This is subjective noise rather than a measurable overlap. The lane format in the fix matches clutter.ts (lanes use points and r, segDist check at src/levels/clutter.ts:79) and src/levels/observatory.ts:26.

findings.title: Sprint dust is opaque, outlined toon spheres up to about 1.2 m wide, so a sprint leaves a trail of 'snowballs'
findings.problem:
'dust' particles use `ico(1)` with `toon(color)`: opaque, lit and outlined. They grow to size×2.8, with the size up to 0.22 m radius (src/render/particles.ts:36, :50). Every sprint step spawns one (src/game.ts:328). Landings spawn 5 and shrugs 4 (src/game.ts:323, :231).

On screen they read as cream eggs or snowballs with dark ink outlines lying on the floor (camera-render-me-51b-crop-dust.jpg). Two big grey outlined balls sit in the Playground win frame (camera-render-pg-46-win-a.jpg). The particle code's own comment (particles.ts:13) says vapour must not read as snowballs, yet dust uses exactly that look. This breaks DR-79 and AGENTS 9 (restrained).
findings.fix: Render dust like smoke: a per-puff MeshBasicMaterial (transparent, depthWrite false, outlineParameters.visible=false). Opacity goes 0.35 → 0 over its life. Cap the size at 0.12 m radius × 1.8 growth. Better still, use a flat ground-aligned soft disc (a radial-gradient alphaMap) at y 0.03.
findings.verify: Retake camera-render-me-51 (a 0.9 s sprint at zoom 17). No outlined sphere is visible, and the puffs are gone 0.8 s after the sprint stops.
findings.verify_reason: src/render/particles.ts:36 builds dust as ico(1) with toon(color), so it is opaque, lit and goes through the OutlineEffect. camera-render-me-51b-crop-dust.jpg shows cream spheres with dark ink outlines on the floor, and pg-46-win-a.png shows big outlined grey balls. Sizing correction: update scales by (1+(1-t)*1.8)*min(1,3t) (particles.ts:50), which peaks at 2.2× when t=1/3, not 2.8×. The largest puff is about 0.22×2.2 = 0.48 m radius, roughly 1 m wide, not 1.2 m. Still far too big and solid.

findings.title: REGRESSION (M7): coffee steam still reads as stacked hard-edged grey balls about 1.5 m wide
findings.problem:
Steam now uses unlit, unoutlined MeshBasic spheres that fade (src/render/particles.ts:31-34, :48-49). Each puff is a uniform-opacity disc with a hard silhouette: opacity up to 0.5 and scale up to size×3.4, about 0.75 m radius. One spawns every 450 ms (src/game.ts coffee burst).

Two or three overlapping puffs read as a stack of grey translucent snowballs above the black machine (camera-render-me-06b-crop-steam.jpg). At the front-left corner a huge pale disc floats over the filing cabinets (camera-render-me-11b-crop-steam.jpg). M7 asked for vapour, not snowballs. This breaks DR-79.
findings.fix: Give the smoke material an alphaMap: a 64×64 canvas radial gradient, white centre to transparent edge, built once and shared. Reduce the peak opacity to 0.28 and the max growth to size×2.2 (about 0.45 m radius). Spawn every 700 ms with a sideways drift of ±0.15 m/s, so puffs separate rather than stack. A camera-facing Sprite with the same gradient works too.
findings.verify: Retake camera-render-me-06 (meeting spawn, zoom 9, yaw toward the coffee corner) after 5 s idle. The steam reads as soft wisps with no visible disc edge (edge-luma step under 8), and no more than 2 puffs overlap.
findings.verify_reason: src/render/particles.ts:31-34 and :48-49: the smoke is an unlit, unoutlined MeshBasic ico with uniform opacity, peaking at about 0.43, and grows to size×3.4 (up to about 0.75 m radius). The coffee machine spawns a puff every 450 ms (src/game.ts:443). camera-render-me-06b-crop-steam.jpg shows overlapping translucent grey discs with hard silhouettes above the machine. It still reads as stacked balls, so M7/DR-79 is not met.

findings.title: Lunch storeroom darkness is still a flat 'lid' plane at 1.5 m that the lamp and stacked boxes poke through (LR1 still open)
findings.problem:
The storeroom is darkened by a translucent plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:64-66). From the kitchen side and in a low orbit it reads as a dark sheet of glass over the room. The floor lamp's pole and 2.2 m shade stick up through it, and box tops above 1.5 m show lit above the sheet (camera-render-lu-55-storeroom-lid-back.jpg, camera-render-lu-05-orbit-low.jpg). In the start view the lamp shade glows above the 'dark' room (camera-render-lu-01-start.jpg).

Raised in R1, R2 P1.9 and QA 12; never fixed. This breaks DR-76.
findings.fix:
Replace the lid with a darkness factor applied in the shader. Add a uniform box (min/max xz of the storeroom) to the toon rim onBeforeCompile (src/render/toon.ts:23) that multiplies outgoingLight by a `uDark` value (0.25 when unlit, 1 when lit) for fragments whose world position lies inside the box. That needs a vWorldPosition varying. Fade uDark to 1 when the portable lamp enters.

Alternatively, keep a plane but put it at y 2.95 (wall-cap height), and lower the lamp and boxes below it.
findings.verify: Retake camera-render-lu-55 and -54 (low orbits) and the start view. No geometry pokes through any dark plane, and the storeroom's interior luma is 35–60% of the corridor's while unlit.
findings.verify_reason: src/lunch-runtime.ts:64-66 creates a PlaneGeometry(8.9,10) at y=1.5, opacity 0.8, with depthWrite false. camera-render-lu-55-storeroom-lid-back.jpg shows a dark glass-like sheet over the storeroom. The floor-lamp pole and shade and the stacked box tops stick up through it, lit. RULES.md DR-76 already lists this as a known issue that was never fixed.

findings.title: Orbiting toward the open front, or spawning near it, frames large areas of void (up to 48% of the start frame)
findings.room: observatory, spectrum, arcade, qfn (start); playground, arcade (zoom 9 front views)
findings.problem:
Rooms have walls on two sides only; the front and right edges are 0.32 m lips (src/levels/decor.ts:66-69). The follow camera centres on Pip with no bounds clamp (src/game.ts:366-368; follow is 1 at the default station zoom of 18.5).

In start frames, the share of dark void pixels is:

| Room | Void share |
|---|---|
| observatory | 48% |
| spectrum | 44% |
| arcade | 32% |
| qfn | 28% |
| lobby | 11% |

In the observatory, the bottom 40% of the screen is empty navy while the receiver and bench are pushed off the top-right (camera-render-ob-01-start.jpg, camera-render-sp-01-start.jpg).

At zoom 9 facing the front, the room ends in a lip and an empty horizon, like a stage with no fourth wall (camera-render-pg-06-zoom9.jpg, camera-render-ar-06-zoom9.jpg). This is DR-75's known 'low lips facing the void'. The start-frame waste is new.
findings.fix:
1. Clamp the follow target. After computing `target`, clamp target.x to ±(W/2 − halfViewX + 1.5) and target.z to the depth range minus halfViewZ, where halfView ≈ distance × tan(fov/2) × aspect × 0.5. When the room is narrower than the view, centre the room instead.
2. Build front and right walls with shellWall() (normals [0,1] and [1,0]). Once the cutaway fix lands they will stub whenever the camera is outside them, so the default camera is unchanged, but a reverse orbit sees a closed room instead of the void.
findings.verify: Recompute the void fraction on camera-render-*-01-start (the python snippet in this review). Every room under 15%. Retake camera-render-pg-06 at zoom 9 facing the front: a wall stub or full wall is visible, not a horizon of void.
findings.verify_reason: camera-render-ob-01-start.jpg has the left third and bottom of the frame as empty navy, with the bench pushed to the top right. My own crude dark-blue pixel count gives about 36% void for the observatory, 36% for spectrum and 14% for the arcade, against the reviewer's 48/44/32%. The numbers depend on the threshold, but the effect is real for the observatory and spectrum. Code: follow = clamp(.62+near*.6) is 1 at zoom 18.5 (near 0.68), and there is no bounds clamp (src/game.ts:366-368). The front and right edges are only 0.32 m lips (src/levels/decor.ts:65-69).
extra_evidence: python luma check on camera-render-ob/sp/ar-01-start.png: void about 0.36/0.36/0.14
findings.fix_correction: Clamp the follow target only while zoomed out (near<0.8), so close follow stays centred on Pip. Also keep Pip's projected position above the bottom action-bar band (NDC y > -0.55), or the clamp will park Pip under the key bar near the front edge. Front and right shellWalls depend on the cutaway fix in finding 0; with the current centre-dot test they would block the default camera.

findings.title: The new rim light has no measurable effect: rim on and ?norim differ by 0.44 mean luma
findings.problem:
The rim term is `rimColor*edge*up*rimStrength*diffuseColor` with rimStrength 0.22, edge = smoothstep(.62,.92,1−N·V) and up = smoothstep(-.2,.6,N.y) (src/render/toon.ts:20-31). Comparing zoom-9 garage frames with and without ?norim: mean absolute luma difference 0.44/255, only 3,415 px differ by more than 10 (mostly animation), and Pip's median luma (180) and darkest 2% (54) are identical (camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-rim.jpg vs -norim.png).

The stated goal, separating props from pale floors (DR-54 asks for at least 25 luma), is not met. Meanwhile the rim forces one custom shader variant onto every toon material. Commit 3631876 marks it 'WIP, verifying'; this is the verification result.
findings.fix:
Either drop the rim (delete rimShader and customProgramCacheKey) or make it do its job. To make it work:
- Set rimStrength to 0.55.
- Widen edge to smoothstep(.45,.85,…).
- Use `up` only to suppress downward faces: smoothstep(-.4,.2,N.y).
- Add the rim to the colour without multiplying by diffuseColor, so dark props also get a light edge.

Then check the rim at grazing silhouettes against pale floors.
findings.verify: Diff ?norim against the default at the same zoom-9 garage view. The mean luma difference on prop silhouettes over the floor must be at least 8 (crop 1-px outline bands). Then check DR-54: props differ from the floor under them by at least 25 luma.
findings.verify_reason: I recomputed the diff from the cited pair (camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-rim.jpg vs -norim.png): mean absolute luma difference 0.43, about 2.4k pixels over 10 (animation included), max 190. The rim term is gated by edge smoothstep(.62,.92), the upward-facing check and a multiply by diffuseColor at strength 0.22 (src/render/toon.ts:21-31). At the game camera it is essentially invisible, so it does not deliver the separation it was added for.

findings.title: Lobby first frame cuts the three left-wall doors, and the title hero crops Pip's waving arm (L1 / P7 re-check)
findings.problem:
- Lobby: at homeZoom 23, yaw 0.14 (src/game.ts:397, :178) the start frame shows the six back-wall doors. The left-wall doors (Fabrication Bay, Signal Observatory, Spectrum Delivery) are cut by the left screen edge and partly covered by the job card (camera-render-lo-01-start.jpg). L1 asked that the first frame show every door.
- Title: the hero shot puts Pip 2.6 m to the right at distance 8 (src/game.ts:376). Pip's waving right mitt and shoulder are cut off at the right edge of the 1440×900 frame (camera-render-lo-70-title.jpg).

The survey does show all nine doors (camera-render-lo-02-survey.jpg).
findings.fix:
- Lobby: use homeZoom 27 and a start yaw of 0.32 so the left wall comes into view, or shift the follow target 2 m toward −x for the hub.
- Title: change the right offset to −2.0 and the distance to 8.8, so Pip, including the raised mitt, sits inside x 0.62–0.92 of the frame.
findings.verify: Retake camera-render-lo-01-start: all 9 door frames are fully visible and none sits under the job card. Retake camera-render-lo-70-title: Pip's mitt bounding box ends at least 40 px from the right edge.
findings.verify_reason: camera-render-lo-01-start.jpg: the left-wall doors (Fabrication Bay, Signal Observatory) are cut by the left edge and partly hidden by the job card. camera-render-lo-70-title.jpg: Pip's raised right mitt is cut off at the right edge, an effect of the -2.6 m right offset and distance 8 (src/game.ts:376). Correction: L1 in the re-check list (RULES.md:507) is 'lobby blade signs and Workshop arch facing forward', not 'the first frame shows every door', so the lobby half is a new P2 rather than an L1 re-check. The centre board lists every room and the survey shows all doors, so this is polish.

findings.title: Orbit pitch has a dead zone at close zoom: the stored pitch clamps to −0.3…0.45, but the effective pitch clamps again to 0.3…1.25
findings.problem:
The pointer and stick update `this.pitch` within [−0.3, 0.45] (src/game.ts:174, :315). updateCamera then computes `clamp(.68−.24*near+this.pitch, .3, 1.25)` (src/game.ts:368).

At zoom 9 (near=1) the base is 0.44, so stored values below −0.14 are clipped to 0.3. The bottom 0.16 rad of the drag range, about 40 px, does nothing. After dragging down fully, the first 40 px of dragging back up don't move the camera, which feels like a stuck control (DR-22). At zoom 38 the steepest view is 1.13 rad, so the player can never look nearly straight down outside the survey.
findings.fix: After computing `base=.68−.24*near`, re-clamp the stored value to `this.pitch=clamp(this.pitch, .3−base, 1.25−base)`, so the stored and effective pitch always agree. Optionally widen the upper bound to 1.35 at zoom ≥30.
findings.verify: Unit test: zoom 9, drag down 400 px, then up 10 px. The camera pitch must change on the first up-move. Repeat at zoom 38.
findings.verify_reason: Measured the settled camera elevation at zoom 9 for stored pitch values. Stored -0.30, -0.25, -0.20, -0.15 and -0.14 all give an elevation of 0.300; -0.10 gives 0.34 and 0 gives 0.44. So 0.16 rad of stored range (40 px at 0.004/px, src/game.ts:174) does nothing. At zoom 38 with stored 0.45 the elevation is 1.13, the maximum. The double clamp is src/game.ts:174/315 against :368.

notes.playability:
The camera is the weakest part of this dimension.

What works:
- Interior walls fade (LR7 at the Lunch kitchen/corridor wall is fixed: camera-render-lu-56).
- The bench camera locks orbit and wheel and snaps to a fixed framing; Esc stands Pip up again.
- Zoom clamps 9..38 as specified.
- No room produced console or page errors in any script.
- The host GPU holds 60 fps in real (non-manual) runs.

What fails:
- Shell-wall cutaway: the centre-direction test leaves a full-height wall between the camera and Pip near corners and along the front half of side walls. Pip disappears completely, or the camera grazes a wall cap (P1).
- Fade coverage: only pillars and interior walls fade, through one ray, so shelves, racks and pillar edges hide Pip (P1, known).
- Survey: the fixed zoom 44 crops the 33 m rooms and is useless in portrait (P1).
- Performance: draw calls are 2.6–4.7× the 500 target, and PROGRESS's 176 figure no longer holds (P1).

The quality bug matters here too. Every first-time player runs at quality 0, so adaptQuality never had a chance to matter.
notes.fun:
Camera presentation of success is uneven.
- The Playground win push-in frames Pip and the lit lamp well, with a confetti burst (camera-render-pg-46-win-a).
- Every station win crops Pip at the boots and frames the bench rather than the robot, cabinets or dish that came to life (P1).
- The arcade play test, the moment that should be funny and rewarding with a kid hammering the cabinet, happens off-screen from the bench view.
- Sprint dust and coffee steam read as snowballs, which undercuts the otherwise clean toon look.
notes.teaching:
From the camera side, the biggest teaching cost is the bench camera. It frames only the tabletop, so the in-world consequence of a fix stays off-screen: the cabinet the kid plays, and the garage robot on its stand partly under the side card. The player learns from the monitor text instead of the world, against DR-28 and DR-47.

The Lunch storeroom lid makes the 'dark storeroom' read as a glass sheet with a lamp poking through, which weakens the 'bring light' cue.
notes.clarity:
What reads well:
- The game camera at default zoom.
- Outlines are genuinely dark (the darkest 2% of a Pip crop measures 54 luma, which passes DR-56).
- No z-fighting or shimmer appeared in settled far or close frames. All diffs were animated actors and HUD (camera-render-pg-40b, camera-render-me-60c).
- Shadows have no visible acne or peter-panning, and the shadow frustum (±20.5/±19) covers even the 33×20 rooms at 4096².

What doesn't:
- Start frames in the observatory and spectrum waste 44–48% of the screen on void, because the follow camera doesn't clamp to the room.
- The lobby's first frame cuts the left-wall doors.
- The survey's corners sit under HUD cards.
- The rim light currently has no visible effect, so it neither helps nor hurts.
notes.models:
Not my dimension, but camera close-ups exposed model-side rendering issues.
- Pillar trims (base, rail, cap) aren't part of the fade, so a faded pillar becomes a glass case whose shelves cut Pip at the waist.
- Dust particles are outlined opaque spheres.
- Steam puffs are hard-edged discs.

Pip, props and fixtures otherwise render cleanly at zoom 9, with no near-plane clipping into props at the bench views: no mesh came within 0.6 m of any bench camera.

All review-5 screenshots taken with cap.mjs fullfx:true were actually at quality 0 (no AO, no bloom, DPR 1) because of the fresh-profile quality bug. Model and art reviewers should know that AO and bloom were never in their frames.
